rationale: The run landed on the Moncler homepage (en-de) where no product tiles exist, hence PLP extraction failed. Moncler often shows a OneTrust cookie banner and sometimes locale/promo modals that can block interactions. Adding consent/modal selectors and a deterministic fallback to a known PLP URL (men down jackets) stabilizes entry. Moncler PDP URLs consistently include '/products/', so using that pattern yields robust PDP link extraction. Additional PLP-ready selectors and PDP price/title fallbacks increase resilience against minor DOM changes. URL rules normalize the locale to en-de, avoid corporate monclergroup.com redirects, and strip marketing params to reduce redirect noise.
code_hints: If landing on the homepage (path = /en-de/), immediately navigate to the seed PLP override (men down jackets) before attempting PLP extraction.
Before any extraction, try clicking cookie consent using selectors in overrides_patch.consent_selectors; ignore errors if not present.
If a modal overlays the page (e.g., locale or promo), try modal_close_selectors before proceeding.
Wait for overrides_patch.wait_for_selectors.plp_ready OR for at least 6 pdp_link matches before considering PLP ready.
For product tiles, prefer anchors matching a[href*='/products/']; derive the card element via anchor.closest('article, li').
On PDP, if visible price selectors fail, read meta[itemprop='price'][content] or parse JSON-LD (script[type='application/ld+json']) for offers.price.
Guard against lazy loading by scrolling incrementally until no new tiles appear twice; then extract.
Only treat a page as PLP if there are 8+ unique PDP links; otherwise follow top-nav links containing /men/ or /women/ and a Jackets/Down keyword.
